info.title: WDX Open APIv1
info.description:
The WDX One system is a Client Lifecycle Management platform built atop Microsoft Dynamics CRM. It offers an Open API to facilitate integration.

- **Swagger** (*/swagger*): A dynamic environment for interacting with the API - provides a real-time interface to send requests, view responses, and understand endpoint behaviours.
- **Stoplight** (*/api-docs*): An alternative read-only view of the API documentation - offers a more structured and detailed documentation layout.

### WDX One and Microsoft Dynamics CRM

The WDX One system is intricately linked with Microsoft Dynamics CRM. While the Open API covers a broad range of functionalities, certain user journey aspects, such as creating and qualifying an Opportunity, are not yet API-driven. These processes require direct interaction through our Angular-based web app. Access this web app via the Microsoft Dynamics CRM interface at Dynamics CRM UI to complete these user journey steps.

## Sandbox

The Sandbox is a replica of the Open API instance that operates independently of the CRM and other system components. This provides an isolated environment for developers to experiment, test, and refine their integration solutions without impacting the live CRM system. The Sandbox:
- Stores data in-memory, allowing for easy data reset.
- Is much faster, as it's self-contained and doesn't interact with external system components.
- Enables coding and automated testing without backend data management concerns.

### Sandbox Features

- **Simulation of Microsoft Dynamics Plugins:** Enables user journeys that depend on plugin-triggered data creation or modification. For instance, creating a Client in the Sandbox triggers a simulated plugin that generates a Suitability Review record, as in the real system. The Suitability Review record for the client can then be queried by another API.
- **Background Jobs Simulation:** This simulates background processes such as "starting" a Suitability Review, which in turn creates Suitability Review Contacts and Suitability Review Portfolios for each relevant Party and Product in the client data structure.

## API Features

### Record collections

Available for certain endpoints returning record collections.

- **Filtering:** Use the `X-Filter` HTTP header to specify conditions for filtering data. The syntax is simple and user-friendly, with the following rules:

    - Only `AND` (`&&`) and `OR` (`||`) operators are supported.
    - Most values (excluding numbers), must be enclosed in quotation marks.
    - Date and time values follow the C# `string.Format` style. When working with date values stored in the CRM, using short date formats (e.g., "2025-11-25") will treat the value as a full calendar date rather than a specific point in time. This means filters such as on, on or before, and on or after will include the entire date, not just the instant at midnight. In this context, the supported comparison operators are: ==, <,>
    , <=, and >=.
    - Multiple fields can be included in a single query.
    - To filter by externald ID use ExternalID subproperty. For instance, in the case of owner it has to be unique across user and team entities
    - `Owner.ExternalId == "ABCBank\\User_Name"`
    - Nested properties are supported for certain fields, such as object history and owner. For example:
    - `Created.On == "2025-01-02" && Created.By.Id == "guid-value-here"`
    - String fields support wildcards for partial matches:
    - `*` can be used to indicate "begins with," "ends with," or "contains."

    **Example Query:**
    ```
    FirstName = "Jo*" && Created.On >= "2025-08-08" && Created.On < "2025-08-09" && Owner.Id != "3eae1051-4b36-ec11-b81f-00505601139e"
    ```

    - **Sorting:** Use the `X-Sort` HTTP header, formatted as a field name and direction (`desc` or `asc`). Refer to the sortable properties for each endpoint in the Swagger documentation.

    `X-Sort: FirstName=desc`

    - **Paging:** Manages large datasets by controlling the size and starting point of the data returned. Utilize `X-Limit` and `X-Offset` headers, accepting integer values.

    `X-Limit: 50, X-Offset: 100`

    ### Background Workload Management

    Facilitates the submission and tracking of background tasks. Submit and query background workloads using the specific API endpoints; each workload requires an entity ID representing the record in the system that the workload is executed against, along with relevant parameters.

    > The "start Suitability Review" job can be initiated via the dedicated API `/suitability-reviews/{id}/start`. The status of the workload can be queried via `/workloads/{workloadId}`

    ### Webhooks

    Allows real-time updates from the system via event subscriptions. Register a webhook through the API by specifying an event type and a callback URL. The available event types are listed under `/webhooks/event-types`

    | Event Type | Description |
    | ----------- | ----------- |
    | SR_STARTED | When a Suitability Review is started for a client, creating the Suitability Review Contacts and Suitability Review Portfolios |

    ## JSON Forms

    JSON Forms is a JSON Schema based approach for creating forms. It comes with off the shelf support for React, Angular and Vue. See more at **[JSON Forms documentation](https://jsonforms.io/docs)**.

    ### Explanation of WDX form frameworks

    > **Dynamic Forms (WDX One):** The WDX One system offers a flexible solution for managing complex data structures and form interactions. These forms can be fully customized to handle various conditions such as field visibility and mandatory checks.
    >
    > **Dynamic Forms (Open API):** This capability is replicated as an Open API feature, supported both in the main API and the Sandbox environment. Therefore, form definitions in WDX One can be published into the Open API.
    >
    > **JSON Forms (Open API)**: To enable standardised integration with UIs, such as Client Portals, the Open API form definitions and data are made available in the **[JSON Forms](https://jsonforms.io/)** standard, so that frameworks such as Angular or React can easily consume them.

    ### JSON Forms APIs

    The relevant APIs for integrating a JSON Forms front-end with the Open API are:

    - **Form Definition IDs**: `/forms/definitions`
    - **JSON Schema** (*form definition*): `/forms/json-schema/{formDefinitionId}`
    - **JSON UI Schema**: `/forms/json-ui-schema/{formDefinitionId}`
    - **JSON Data**: `/forms/json-data/{formDefinitionId}/{entityId}`

    > The relevant form definition ID can be found from the `/forms/definitions` API by identifying an ID for a given form name, such as **"AML"** (`entityId` will be a Suitability Review Contact record) or **"SRP"** (`entityId` will be a Suitability Review Portfolio record).

    ### JSON Forms visualiser

    **WDX.One.Tools.JsonFormsApp** is a locally-run Angular app that serves as a developer tool to demonstrate use of **[JSON Forms Core](https://github.com/eclipsesource/jsonforms/tree/master/packages/angular)** to consume the WDX JSON Forms APIs. Use this to view and save forms in WDX One.

    ## Visual Studio Connected Services

    **[Visual Studio Connected Services](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/generating-http-api-clients-using-visual-studio-connected-services/)** makes use of NSwag for generating strongly-typed clients from OpenAPI specification documents:

    - Download the Open API definition **[swagger.json](/v1/swagger.json)**
    - Follow the steps **[here](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/generating-http-api-clients-using-visual-studio-connected-services/)** to generate a .NET client.
    - Instantiate an `HttpClient` and set the authentication header with an access token.
    - Use the generated client (`swaggerClient`) to interact with the Open API.

    ```csharp
    var token = "<access token>
        ";
        var apiUrl = "<Open API base URL>
            "; // excluding "/openapi"

            var httpClient = new HttpClient();
            httpClient.BaseAddress = new Uri(apiUrl);
            httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);

            var client = new swaggerClient(httpClient);
            ```

            ## Example Journeys
            ### Individual Onboarding

            | Action | API |
            |---|---|
            | Create Person or Organisation | POST   /v1/persons, POST /v1/organisations |
            | Create/Update Contact Point | POST   /v1/contact-points/{emails/phones/postal-addresses}, PATCH /v1/contact-points/{id} |
            | Create Prospect | POST   /v1/prospects |
            | Create PartyToClientRole | POST   /v1/party-to-client-roles |
            | Create Portfolio | POST   /v1/products |
            | Create Opportunity | POST   /v1/opportunity |
            | Qualify Opportunity | POST   /v1/processes/progress-process |
            | Read Suitability Review for Prospect | GET   /v1/prospects/{id}/suitability-reviews |
            | Read Suitability Review Contacts and Suitability Review Portfolios for Suitability Review  | GET   /v1/suitability-reviews/{id} |
            | Read Form Definitions | GET   /v1/forms/definitions, GET /v1/forms/definitions/{id} |
            | Update KYC data for Suitability Review Contact | PATCH   /v1/forms/data/{formDefinitionId}/{suitabilityReviewContactId} |
            | Update AML data for Suitability Review Contact | PATCH   /v1/forms/data/{formDefinitionId}/{suitabilityReviewContactId} |
            | Update Suitability data for Suitability Review Portfolio | PATCH   /v1/forms/data/{formDefinitionId}/{suitabilityReviewPortfolioId} |
            | Complete Processes | POST   /v1/processes/progress-process |

            ### Progress A Process
            | Action | API |
            |---|---|
            | Read Process Types | GET   /v1/process-types |
            | Read Processes for Target | GET   /v1/processes/by-target/{targetId} |
            | Progress Process | POST   /v1/processes/progress-process |
            | Check Current Step | GET   /v1/processes/{id} |
